h.strategy: Measured interaction effects are dominated by a few robust regularities: an edit's effect is larger when the parent is weak overall and smaller when the parent is already strong (ceiling and floor); a component's removal costs less when another component already fills the same role; and an edit's effect changes most when the conditioning field controls the main bottleneck. Build each hypothesis on one of these, stated as a specific conditional. Prefer conditions that change overall parent quality substantially over conditions with subtle effects. Do not chase counterintuitive sign reversals. Spread hypotheses across different edited and conditioning fields, and use both HIGHER and LOWER directions roughly equally.

hyps.why: Replacing a dead edge with a 3x3 conv adds much more than replacing an existing op, which is often already a useful one.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1 and 2 and the 1->3 path, so reviving it from none gives a large gain.
Turning on the 2->3 edge with a conv from none opens a new learnable path into the output.
With edge 1 also removed, edge 0 is the only route into nodes 1 and 2, so removing it hurts far more.
Adding a direct residual path gives a big gain over no direct edge, but a smaller one over most other existing ops.
Adding a skip into the output from none gives a clear gain over replacing an existing op.
With edge 1 absent, edge 0 is the sole feature route into nodes 1 and 2, so a strong conv there matters more.
Upgrading from 1x1 to 3x3 conv gives a smaller gain than filling an empty or weak slot.
Removing edge 5 costs less when a strong direct conv into the output already fills its role.
Removing 1->3 is less harmful when the direct 0->3 edge is a strong conv.
